document:
Allow motorcycles to have auxiliary flashing lights, Please amend the Road Vehicles Lighting Regulations 1989 (Section 13, Para 2), to allow Motorcycles to have, in addition to their steady state headlamps, 'auxiliary flashing lights' to make it easier for other road users to better see approaching motorcycles, the same as for pedal cycles currently., Some research has found that flashing lights make it easier to detect other road users, such as cyclists.
 
We believe this change could help reduce the number of vehicle and motorcycle incidents where vehicle drivers pull out in front of approaching motorcycles because they did not see the approaching motorcycle.

Require Braille labelling on all products in the United Kingdom, I would like the Government to introduce legislation to require manufacturers include Braille labelling on all products sold in the UK. This should include medication, which should have all relevant information - including dosage - in braille., Too often, the blind and visually impaired have to rely on someone else to read labels in shops and choose things for us. We do not want this. We want independence and in order to have that independence, we need all products clearly labelled in Braille. This should be mandatory under the Equality Act 2010.

Make a driving licenses mandatory for electrical scooters, Electrical scooters can be dangerous, for the drivers, for the pedestrians, for the animals and the surroundings where most vehicles are not allowed., They are often driven carelessly on the pavements at high speeds, can be used by thieves to get away, and can cause life-threatening accidents.
 
We want the Government to make having a full driving licence a requirement for anyone who uses an electronic scooter, to improve the safety and wellbeing of communities where these are used.

Require all cycles to have registration plates, Call for submissions to relevant Committee and collect evidence concerning injuries/fatalities caused by cyclists together with statistics on cyclists prosecuted for breaching road laws, I have had several friends who have suffered injuries due to cyclists failing to stop at pedestrian crossings and have , myself, been injured by a cyclist riding on the footpath 
Cycles should be regarded as road vehicles and be able to be identified by registration plate in the case of anyone witnessing dangerous cycling behaviour

Raise The Trading Schemes Regulations 1997 £200 'liability limit' to £750, This petition is a request to raise the £200 liability limit in Section 10 of The Trading Schemes Regulations 1997 to £750 to reflect inflation since this legislation was passed, whilst retaining protection for scheme participants., The existing limit is now 25 years old!
 
The current legislation reads:
 
10. A promoter of, or a participant in, a trading scheme shall not accept from a participant joining the trading scheme any payment or an undertaking to make a payment of any sum exceeding £200 unless 7 days have expired from the making of the agreement relating to goods or services supplied or to be supplied under that agreement to the participant by the promoter or any other participant under the trading scheme.

Limit penalty charge notices (PCNs) for traffic offences to £20, We want all PCNs that local authorities are able to issue for traffic offences to be limited to £20., We believe many PCNs are too expensive, and can amount to a person's entire daily. This is especially unfair for minor offences. Therefore, all PCNs should be restricted to a maximum of £20.
 
As inflation rises and economic conditions worsen, limiting fines like this should help reduce the financial burden on people who are already struggling to make ends meet.

Raise the speed limit to 80mph on motorways, I would like the Government to increase the speed limit on motorways to 80mph. Because if we could go faster we could get around the country quicker and deliveries can be made faster.,

Adjust the MOT requirement for a manufacturer fitted airbag to be present., Under the current MOT regulations the removal of manufacturer fitted airbags is classed as a major defect. This makes it difficult to fit a racing type steering wheel to a vehicle and have it remain road-legal, this is restrictive to those who wish to use their car for both sport and leisure., We would like a provision included in the MOT test to allow the removal of manufacturer fitted airbags in cars with bucket seats and harnesses (both legal modifications under MOT guidelines and usually the minimum requirement for motorsports events) as these types of safety systems are designed to be used without an airbag in place. This will allow those who are interested in using their car in a sporting capacity to make changes to their steering wheel while keeping the car road legal.

Carry out an independent review into Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (LTNs), The review should look at, but not be limited to, possible benefits and disbenefits they might have to the local and wider area where they are introduced. This should including pollution, road safety, mental wellbeing, effects on the vulnerable, and congestion. Both inside and outside an LTN., Many residents that live on the boundaries of these LTNs experience increased congestion, road traffic accidents, pollution, damage to their mental wellbeing, and feel like they are not being listened to or consulted.

Exempt organisers of motorsport events on public roads from legal liabilities, 
We want laws and regulations governing the legal liabilities for motorsport events on public roads changed, so that the organisers of these events have no legal liability of personal injury and/or loss of damages.
, The sport of motor racing on public roads has been around for over a hundred years on British roads. Now with changing times, the cost of organising these events have increased due to insurance costs etc.
 
We want public liability laws to be changed regarding organised motorsport on public roads, so that liability for personnel injury or loss of damages will lie inevitably in the hands of spectators and/or riders. Therefore the organisers will be exempt from any legal liability, provided that the organiser/s has demonstrated that appropriate precautions and warnings were in place to communicate dangerous events being performed (warnings stating: anyone attending the event will be there at their own risk.)

Raise the Speed limit on Motorways from 70mph to 90mph, The 70mph speed limit on motorways was introduced in 1965. Since then the technology and safety features of cars has come on considerably. We believe it is now safe for cars to drive at this speed, and this should be recognised. It could also help to reduce congestion on motorways.,

Require councils remove LTNs and underused bike lanes that lack public support, Require local authorities (LAs) remove low traffic neighbourhoods (LTNs) and underused bike lanes that lack public support. Change guidance from assuming they remain to requiring removal, unless, in 3 months, the LA can show > 50% approval, using broad, unbiased, independent, local opinion research., There's widespread anger at LTNs and other congesting traffic schemes but LAs are not removing them due to statutory guidance and the money they make.

Many were built with no proper consultation as a pandemic measure; but it is over.

We believe these schemes, often justified by doubtful green claims, undermine the law obliging LAs to expedite traffic flow; and create social division, ghettos, gridlock and local economic damage.

The attack on liberty and persecution of motorists is unfair and must stop.

Fund improvements to Junction 5 of the M27, We want the Government to provide dedicated funding for National Highways to improve Junction 5 of the M27., Current traffic at this junction can cause delays of up to 1 hour, affecting workers, students and more.

Make it a legal requirement push bikes to be insured and show a number plate, All cyclists should have lights, insurance and a number plate if using the road, for the protection of other vehicles. All cyclists should show a registration on their cycles as to be identified, so that they can be more easily identified if they break the law., All motor vehicles that use the road have to by law be insured. Why should cyclists not be subject to the same requirement? They don't pay road tax as it is but we believe it is not fair that they also don't need to be insured. If all cyclists had a visible registration on their bicycles, like motor vehicles have to, then they could be more easily identified by CCTV or law enforcement if breaking the law. Such as going through red lights and riding on the pavements

Increase mobility scooter max speed limit on roads to 15.5mph to equal e-bikes, The current maximum speed for a mobility scooter is 8mph on the road. We believe this is unfair since e-bikes can be motor assisted up to 15.5mph. Mobility scooters should be given the same speed limit., We believe 8mph is dangerously slow on de-restricted roads and lanes. I would like the Government to bring the maximum speed up to 15.5mph, even if need be by creating a new type of category. The current law has two classes of mobility scooter in order keep things safe and easy. The Government could create a third class with max speed of 15.5mph in line with e-bikes and e-scooters, and also to bring the max speed in line with many European countries of where the max speed is set to around 15mph.

Make a legal requirement for cyclist to wear helmet cameras, Too many motorists get away with breaking the law because they can't be identified. We want the Government to require cyclists to wear helmet cameras, to help the police identify and take action against motorists who break the law, especially where this involves vulnerable road users, like cyclists.,

Continue the Office for National Statistics’ COVID-19 Infection Survey, Since mass testing stopped, the ONS’ COVID-19 Infection Survey has remained the only reliable source of information on the level of prevalence of COVID-19 in the U.K. population. This information has been vital to helping those who are clinically vulnerable plan around high infection rates., Continue funding and running the study for at least an additional year, even with a smaller population size.

Make it unlawful to wear full face coverings in public, It is crucial to create a policy that makes it unlawful to wear full face coverings, such as balaclavas, in public. Many young people wear these masks to feel included in their group of friends, or to disguise themselves when they engage in offensive behaviour., They can make it difficult for victims to recognise offenders and can spread fear among children and vulnerable groups of people.

Reduce the national speed limit for rural roads to 30mph, The Government should reduce the national speed limit on rural roads to 30mph, to better protect pedestrians, cyclists, horse riders and wildlife, as well as drivers themselves. It could also reduce damage to roads and cars., 60% of people killed on Britain's roads die on rural roads. Following a THINK! survey 25% of drivers admitted having a near miss on a country road whilst 40% have been surprised by an unexpected hazard. A third confessed to taking a bend too fast. These roads are more likely to be single lane with hazards such as sharp bends, foliage, horse riders and walkers with no pavement to use. A 30mph speed limit could help reduce serious injuries and deaths on country roads.

We call upon the Government to launch an investigation into the A585 Bypass Road, We call upon the Government to launch an investigation into the planning and execution of the A585 bypass that is currently under construction near Blackpool by Kier via National Highways., We believe that the new bypass road has not been properly thought out, planned or executed. We don't believe credible traffic data has been collected and that incorrect traffic modelling has been used, and is resulting in a shocking waste of public funds and a total shambles of modifications to our roads, that is causing ridiculous knock effects to even short journeys and impacting all our lives.

Allow National Highways officers to use blue lights and speed in emergencies, Give National Highways traffic officers the ability to use blue warning lights and exceed the speed limit to a maximum of 90mph to access time critical incidents. With more Smart Motorways, HATOs need the tools to gain access to incidents quicker and save lives. Saving lives should be a priority., Even though National Highways Traffic Officers are often first on the scene of incidents on the strategic road network, dealing with anything from debris in the road which could cause an accident to major Road Traffic Collisions, they cannot use blue warning lights or exceed the speed limit. If you break down in a live lane, believe it or not, they have to stick to the speed limit, even when it's reduced for emissions!

Allow the NATO medal issued for Operation Cabrit to be worn by service members, Service personnel are enduring a long six months on Operation Cabrit on behalf of NATO's EFP across the Baltics, with basic food, in a camp isolated from a lot of the population of the JOA. NATO are issuing a medal, but British service members are not allowed to display this on their uniforms., I would like the Government to allow British service personnel to display this medal, as service members involved in this operation are not living in the best location, in the best conditions, and get no extra money to make the tour and be separated from their loved ones, but still go through the tour, only to be unable to display the medal NATO are issuing. We want the Government to add this medal to the list of NATO-issued medals that British service members are allowed to display on their uniforms.

Strictor road limits, parking limits and speed camera on Mollison Way HA8 5QX, We need more stricter road limits and speed cameras on Mollison Way HA8 5QX to protect residents and build a safer neighnourhood. Currently, reckless drivers are abusing the street to be a race track. The road is not safe for other drivers, pedestrians or residents.,

Introduce offences of Death by Careless/Dangerous Cycling, We want the Government to introduce offences of Death by Careless/Dangerous Cycling, with penalties equivalent to those for Death by Careless/Dangerous Driving. Currently only offences with lower maximum penalties apply to cases where a cyclists causes the death of a pedestrian or other road user., I have lost my son in a fatal accident due to a cyclist cutting in front of him at a filter light. The cyclist was found guilty of careless and inconsiderate cycling and received a fine. There is NO law for cyclists to be charged with Death by Careless/Dangerous Cycling, and we want this to change.

Introduce statutory licensing and regulation of builders, There are few options for people to seek redress for poor workmanship by builders and it is too easy for builders to avoid liabilities by liquidating one company and starting another. An increase in people claiming to be competent builders with the only intention to con families out of their money., Current protection for consumers are inadequate, leaving victims who have been scammed or left with poor or dangerous workmanship at the hands of rogue builders unprotected. It's too easy for a rogue builder to prey on homeowners and the few avenues of redress are costly for victims.

Private hire licensing councils to have permanent enforcement in each area, Have any local council that issues a private hire license to either limit its license to operating borders, or have enforcement in each operating area where that license is in use., Public Saftey.
There is a spread in the areas in which out of district private hire vehicles are being used, this is leading to operators/drivers of such licensed vehicles working areas a long way from where they were licensed.
In some cases the owner/drivers of the vehicles are breaching the legislated rules at the moment by not using the correct signage and pretending to be hackney vehicles and are operating without insurance.
We need local enforcement covering ALL areas the license covers.

ban supermarkets charging extra for item if a person doesn't have a loyalty card, we want the goverment to force a rule that no supermarket can charge extra if the person doesn't have a loyalty card.
you have to be over 18 to obtain a loyalty card and making it so everyone under that age has to pay the over inflated prices that the supermarkets are charging., we want low prices for all customers, not just for those that use one of the said cards.

Only require learner drivers to retake the part of a theory test they fail, It’s annoying when you take your theory test and you pass one section (eg. hazard perception) and fail the other (eg. multiple choice questions) and you have to retake both parts. You shouldn’t have to redo both when you have already passed one section., I want the Government to change this, so if you get over the pass mark on either multiple choice questions or hazard perception but not the other you should only have to redo the one you didn’t get the pass mark for.

Cyclists must have a bell and must use it to warn pedestrians of their presence, With so many cycle lanes, the Government must implement clearer rules. Some cyclists do not adhere to speed limits. Cyclists often go at speed and without bells. This can often result in heated encounters and has potential for accidents., I believe the Highway Code now favours cyclists to the detriment of pedestrians, especially regarding the use of shared pathways. Much of the Highway Code is merely advisory to cyclists including the use of a 'bell'. The HC states: "...slow down when necessary ... let [pedestrians] know you are there; eg., by ringing your bell (it is recommended that a bell is fitted to your bike), or by calling out politely.... do not pass pedestrians at high speed...".

Ban the display of medication on shop floors, We want the Government to prevent medication - such as paracetamol - from being displayed on the shop floor, where it is easy to reach and steal by children and adults, and make it so it can only be accessed from a pharmacy counter.,

Introduce a temporary Blue Badge scheme, Currently eligibility for Blue Badges is linked to the permanence of a disability or condition. There are children and adults that require wheelchairs or walking aides for periods of less than three years and can't manage without use of disabled parking. , The Government should update its guidance to include temporary disabilities and allow for temporary disabled blue badges to be issued for periods up to one year.

Require motorcyclists to wear high visibility clothing, We want the Government to make it a legal requirement for motorcyclists to wear high visibility clothing whilst driving on UK roads., We believe this could help reduce the number of collisions and fatalities involving motorcycles.

Make 12 the legal age to be on the back of a motorbike, In some countries there is a legal limit on the age of 12 years old for when a child can be a passenger on a motorbike. In this country we have no legal limit which puts children of younger ages at risk! I want the government to impose a legal age for people riding on the back of motorbikes. , I believe with the rising costs of living more and more people are using motorbikes as a cheaper alternative to cars and I have seen a dramatic change in the amount of children as young as 5/6 on the back of bikes going to school and driving around with hardly any regulations to keep them safe. Please change the legal age to 12 years old the same as some other countries.

Exchange of driving licences issued in Republic of Moldova to UK driving license, I want to draw your attention to the fact that you have made a decision to accept the exchange of driving licenses of other countries such as Ukrainian into UK equivalent driving licenses. I believe that the citizens of the Republic of Moldova are around 500,000 and they deserve this. Thank you.,

Increase e-bike maximum assisted speed from 15.5mph to 20mph, After 15.5mph e-bikes can be ridden quicker, but the rider will no longer receive assistance from the motor., We ask Government to consider adjusting the limits to be in line with US legislation of 20mph, which will also allow cyclists to move away from dangers more quickly.

Require CBT, licence, insurance and helmet to ride e-bikes and e-scooters, Electric bike and scooter users should have compulsory basic training, be licensed and insured to protect third parties. Helmets should be required by law to protect drivers. This would match requirements for mopeds and light motorcycles., I have personally witnessed e-scooters being driven with multiple people on, a car being trashed, and an electric bike travelling through a park at speed, which nearly collided with my dog.

Ban the sale of fireworks to the general public, Purchasing and owning fireworks should not be allowed for the general public. The Government should introduce a law stating that fireworks should only be permitted for professional shows and events - this will mean they are handled safely, cleanly, and at predictable times., The negatives of fireworks outweigh the positives. Every year fireworks do the following: 

- Stress out animals, often to point of causing death 
- Trigger people with PTSD and trauma (e.g. soldiers)
- Harm those with sensory issues, due to the unpredictable noise
- Cause litter that is then left to rot
- Flood our already stretched A&Es with unnecessary injuries

I understand that they look pretty, however they do more damage than good. Pro shows enable people to still enjoy them, just considerately.

Require schools allow students to wear shorts and tracksuits., I want the government to require schools to allow students to wear shorts in extreme hot weathers and tracksuits in cold weather., As from experience the temperature has severely impacted my education as it makes it harder to fully concentrate. The temperature does not only impact my learning, it also impacts other pupils' learning. I also want to make students reach their maximum potential and for them to be able to learn without anything getting in their way.

Make dash cams a legal requirement, Make dash cams a legal requirement for vehicles on the road., When vehicles are involved in accidents, a dash cam would make it easier to find out exactly what happened.

Take action to restrict online access to pornography strictly to over 18s, Studies show that pornography can have serious adverse effects on individuals and their relationships. It is too easy for under 18s to access pornography online, and we want the Government to take action to ensure that it can only be accessed by over 18s., Online pornography should only be accessible using a Government-issued password or key code that is issued to over 18s. Making pornography available without a requirement to provide this should be a criminal offence.
 
We also want the Government to run a public awareness campaign about the dangers and risks of using pornography.

Change school transport guidance to recognise children may have multiple homes, Currently the statutory guidance for school transport states that a child’s home is defined as “the place where he/she is habitually and normally resident.” This should be changed to recognise children may have multiple homes., Local Authorities (LAs) should be required to provide home school transport for eligible children who reside at more than one home formally as a result of parents who co-parent but do not live together. The definition of home being one residence is no longer the norm. Many eligible children can often only access education when at the residence recognised by the LA as the home. When the child is at their ‘other home’ they don’t receive transport, preventing access to education.

Nationalise all public transport and make it free for everyone at all times,  
Much "public" transport is owned by companies running it for profit. It can be expensive and unreliable, making it an unviable alternative to cars for most people.


Nationalise public transport and make all journeys free, to discourage car use, encourage exercise and boost the economy., For more information read this article: "The Case for Making Public Transit Free Everywhere: From Spain to Germany and Luxembourg to Estonia, more and more countries are experimenting with fare-free transportation": https://www.wired.co.uk/article/free-public-transit

Save Maryport Pool Project, Maryport in Cumbria has no public or private swimming pool in the town or immediate area. Funds have been specifically allocated under the levelling up criteria/ regeneration for the development of a swimming pool., The Council have decided not to go ahead with the pool project development due to concerns around the financial running costs and have not released the report for public scrutiny! The community deserves to be enabled to gain the opportunity to have a swimming pool developed in the town 
The swimming pool based at Netherhall School foreclosed to make way for the new swimming pool project within the town. The Green policy, Sustainable Development strategies can be used to reduced running costs and revise the current business plan.

Hold a referendum on whether to make photo identity cards compulsory in the UK, The Government should hold a referendum on whether to introduce requirements for every citizen in the country to hold compulsory identification, in the form of a photo identity card, similar to other countries. , This should include a fingerprint, National Insurance Number and NHS number, DOB, and place of birth. I believe that we are becoming a state where scammers, spammers, and hoaxers are getting away with crime with impunity.

Automatically upgrade A2 motorcycle licence to A after 2 years, Now that we have left the EU, we should go back to previous law (pre-2013) whereby motorcycle licenses were automatically upgraded from an A2 licence to an unrestricted licence after two years. Riders should have learned the necessary skill in these two years to ride bigger bikes., We believe taking the same Mod1/Mod2 tests a second time, just on a different capacity bike, doesn't make any difference to training or safety standards.

In the past, an A2 rider would be restricted to two years before achieving a full unrestricted motorcycle license. I propose we now return to that scheme again.

For car drivers of any age or experience, once a full license is obtained, they are able to drive any capacity car of their choosing. This is discrimination against motorcyclists.

INCREASE OF SPEED LIMIT ON MOTORWAYS AND DUAL CARRIAGEWAYS, Fully review the capabilities (or data obtained through manufacturer testing) of modern vehicles such as stopping distances (wet/dry) from a broad spectrum of vehicle manufacturers and review the UK speed limits on all roads in line with the new data., Vehicles of today have a greater performance in speed, stopping distance and safety than the vehicles around the time the current speed limits were set. The increase has specifically been sought on roads with multiple lanes.

Allow all on-call emergency personnel to use green lights on personal vehicles, I would like the Government to change legislation regarding lighting for all on-call emergency personnel. All on-call emergency responders should be allowed (with proof they are an on-call emergency worker) to have green warning lights fitted and authorised to use on their personal vehicles. , I believe introducing this change could reduce response times for on-call emergency responders responding to station or a scene as green lights would show the importance of the emergency workers journey. It could also allow casualties and emergencies to be tended to in a much quicker manner and could also help if they were the first ones on a scene at a road side and would need to make other drivers aware that there is an ongoing incident and to proceed past the on-call vehicle with caution.

Require all motor vehicles have speed limiters fitted, I want the Government to make it mandatory for motor vehicles to have speed limiters fitted, so that they cannot exceed the maximum legal speed limit. I am sick of seeing drivers exceeding the speed limit, with some going 85mph or even faster on motorways., This should help reduce road traffic collisions, especially on motorways. Ensure every vehicle cannot exceed the speed limit. The faster the speed , the less chance of surviving an accident. Let's stop idiot drivers exceeding the speed limit.

Raise the UK Motorway Speed Limit to 80mph, Raising the UK motorway speed limit to 80mph could bring the UK in line with other countries, reduce journey times, and increase efficiency for drivers. With modern cars capable of traveling safely at higher speeds, an increase in the speed limit could reflect current driving practices., Alignment with other countries: Many countries, including France, Germany, and Italy, have speed limits of 80mph on their motorways. 

By increasing the speed limit, drivers could maintain a more consistent speed, this could reduce the risk of accidents caused by sudden braking or abrupt lane changes.

Reduced carbon emissions: By reducing travel times, an increase in the speed limit could lead to fewer carbon emissions and help to tackle climate change.

Fund protective and defensive equipment for paramedics and ambulance crews, The Government should fund protective and defensive equipment for paramedics and crew members, such as stab vests and pepper spray to ensure the most possible safety in difficult situations and environments. Due to the rise in abusive and threating situations., Paramedics and crew have to put themselves into life threatening situations, the requirement of stab vests is crucial in cases where knives are used, however a majority don’t have this protection. In Feb 2022 the Association of Ambulance Chief Executives said "every day last year, a staggering 32 ambulance staff were abused or attacked - more than one during every hour of every day throughout the whole year; a total of 11,749 staff. This was an increase of 4,060 incidents over the last 5 years.

Make it mandatory for Supermarkets to donate unsold food
, Following the example set by the French government, all supermarkets should be required to donate unsold food stuffs so they can be provided to to those in need, rather than being wasted., This would serve the dual purpose of reducing waste and helping those experiencing or facing hunger.
 
There are multiple reasons why we need to act on food wastage and poverty. The rising cost of living is hitting families hard when it comes to providing for young children, and indeed parents themselves working longer and harder to meet rising bills. Requiring supermarkets to donate food stuffs would help enable those in hardship to collect unused food stuffs, reducing waste and helping to tackle hunger.

Require moped/motorcycle making delivers to have a full licence, We want the Government to require drivers using mopeds and motorcycles for deliveries - such as Uber Eats and Deliveroo drivers - to be required to have a full licence., Many delivery drivers use vehicles with L plates and I have seen many driving recklessly, which endangers other road users, pedestrians and themselves. Please pass legislation to stop people making deliveries using mopeds and motorcycles with L plates.

To seek a referendum on the question of dis-establishing, devolved Government., To rescind the Provisions of the Wales Act 1978 taking into account the vote result of that referendum.
Remove the Government of Wales Act 1998 which provided the legal basis for the National Assembly for Wales., Since the commencement of the Welsh Assembly at the Senedd in Cardiff (1988) Welsh people, across the board, have gained zero benefits as a devolved Principality.
Recent laws passed by the Senedd, due to an ongoing, overwhelming one-party State situation, have not been mindful of the overwhelming needs of the people of Wales, and consultation is non-existent.
The Senedd has become a dictatorial, one-party entity, refusing to take note of, nor seek debate or consensus from, the people of Wales.

Create list of ID that premises are required to accept that includes PASS cards, The government should create a list of identification that premises are required to accept that includes the PASS card, CitizenCard and Young Scot card. These should be accepted by entertainment venues and providers of other age-restricted goods and services (including doorstep delivery companies)., We think that currently, unwarranted refusal to accept PASS cards jeopardises access to age-restricted premises and goods for young adults. Encouraging wider acceptance by the police and retail groups will help prevent harm to young people.

Ban cyclists from using a handheld mobile phone/electronic device while cycling, We want a complete ban on the use of a mobile phones or tablet (in the users hand) whilst using an electric bike, or standard pedal bike. This law is already in place for motorists., A cyclist on an electric bike, traveling on a road, cycle lane or path, should not be allowed use their mobile phone / have a mobile phone in their hand. It can be extremely dangerous, and too many accidents are happening on a daily basis, many caused by couriers.

Legalise private e-scooters on public roads and bike lanes, The government should allow e-scooters to be ridden on public roads and bike lanes., I believe it is unfair that people are getting their private e-scooters seized by the police, because they are only allowed to the driven on private land. What is the point of owning an e-scooter if you can’t ride it in public?

DVLA communications to include a reminder to check updates to the Highway Code, Require the DVLA to remind road users that they should re-read the Highway Code regularly and ensure that they are aware of updates. An additional line to be added in all communications, e.g. 'car tax' demands, with a weblink to the most recent Highway Code and any updates., A large proportion of road users seem unaware of (or largely ignore) changes to the Highway Code. There are many reports of incidents from vulnerable road users including walkers, cyclists, horse riders/drivers and motorbike riders e.g. 68 horses were killed on roads in 2022 (British Horse Society data). Campaigns such 'Pass Wide And Slow' and 'Dead Slow' raise awareness but most often amongst affected groups rather than the majority of drivers.

A reminder may encourage drivers to check changes.

Stop the reduction in speed limits to 20 mph in Wales, The decision to reduce speed limits in Wales, has not been properly consulted upon.

We call on the UK Government to order a Judicial Review of the Welsh Government’s decision to reduce speed limits to 20mph on restricted roads or use its own powers to overturn the decision.,

Paint all ULEZ, LEZ and CAZ cameras and poles bright Orange, I would like to see all ULEZ, LEZ and CAZ cameras, poles and feeder pillars to be painted bright orange, I would like this done for 3 reasons, number 1 being that they are easier for drivers to see, 2 easier for visually impaired people to see and 3 so that are distinguished from speed cameras, The current ULEZ cameras and poles are black making them hard to see when driving and walking especially for visually impaired pedestrians, some of the equipment has been poorly placed in the middle of pavements and footpaths risking a person falling over them, walking into them, cycling into them or in some cases accidentally driving into them

Change the maximum pedal assist speed of electric bicycles from 15.5mph to 20mph, The maximum speed an electric bike can go is 15.5mph with pedal assist before it cuts out and this should be increased to 20mph like in the USA. When riding an electric bike I often get overtaken by cyclists on non pedal assist bikes and shows that the speed for pedal assist should change., Electric Bikes (EAPC) are a way of getting people off cars and on bikes. They strike a perfect balance between keeping fit and getting from A to B. Cars are the leading cause of pedestrian deaths in the UK and it is vital we encourage people to get onto two wheels. Many people view cycling as a form of leisure and we think that electric bikes still promote fitness and leisure and also encourage people to switch from cars since they reduce the physical demands of cycling.

Stop family homes being converted into HMO's (House in Multiple Occupation), In our area, almost every time a house goes up for sale it is bought by investors and changed into an HMO with no regard to the local community. Currently, in a stretch of 10 properties, there is now only one family house left. The wider picture needs to be looked at before the plans are passed.,

Increase minimum fine for cyclists failing to stop at red lights to £5,000, Too many cyclists run red lights every day at great risk to pedestrians. This is simply unacceptable. Cyclists do not pay vehicle tax like other road users, so should face serious financial penalties for breaking traffic rules by running red lights., We believe that increasing the minimum fine for this offence would make it clear that cyclists must obey the law, and will face serious penalties for not doing so.

Set vehicle tax rates for motorcycles based on emissions not engine size, Motorcycles are taxed on the size of engine, whereas cars are taxed based on their emissions. We believe this puts people off using motorcycles as a means of transport, and that vehicle tax rates for motorcycles should be based on emissions, not engine size, in line with rates for cars., Setting vehicle tax rates for motorcycles based on emissions could increase the use of motorcycles. It makes sense to look at how to reduce congestion on the roads by reforming vehicle licence rates for motorcycles, so that lower emission vehicles are cheaper to use.

Require cyclists to have visible identification number and insurance
 
, We want the Government to require all cyclists to have a visible identification number and insurance. This would help ensure they can be identified if they break the law, and that insurance is in place to cover any damages or injuries caused by the cyclist., Too many cyclists run red traffic lights, speed and cycling the wrong way on one-way roads.
 
Without any visible form of identification it is difficult for cyclists to be held accountable for road traffic offences, and if they cause an accident it is easy for them to cycle away without being held responsible.

Increase the Minimum Wage for Licensed Security Workers to £14 an Hour, Security professionals are essential to our safety, but some struggle to make ends meet. I believe that increasing the minimum wage is not only fair but also an investment in public security. , Reasons for this increase:

Require tradespeople to be registered , The Government should require all tradespeople to be registered legally before practising, therefore helping to stop people being conned out of their money and having half-finished and inadequate jobs being undertaken., I live in a district where we are constantly being pestered with unqualified workmen asking ridiculous prices, we have just parted with £1,000 for five hours work done by a so called gardener.

England Not to adopt the new 20mph Road speed  limits in the future, Not to consider in changing the majority of 30mph roads in England to 20mph like in Wales., The government must rule out in following Wales in there disastrous new 20 mph speed limit changes .

Regulate & Monitor Gel Nail Products (monomers) sold to the general public., It has been reported amongst the media & scientific literature that there is a significant increase in adverse reactions to gel nail products. Require Highways England to improve A road safety, We think the government should require Highways England to ensure that all A roads score a 4 or 5 on the iRAP star rating system., For example, one road that needs improvement is the A13, which is one of the main routes joining London to Essex. Review access to neuropsychology services , I want the government to look into access to NHS neuropsychology services across England. Reduce penalty for speeding in a 20mph zone to 1 point, if speed is up to 30mph, I want the fixed penalty for speeding in 20mph zone to be reduced to a level I believe commensurate with the offence and more in line with public opinion, if the recorded speed is 30mph or less., Introduction of new 20mph speed limits is I believe the reason for the great increase in the number of speeding offences, while the 12-point level at which motorists lose their licence (and possibly their livelihood) has remained unchanged.

Build the HS2 rail project and the Northern Powerhouse Rail in full, The current Conservative Government should unequivocally commit to completing the High Speed Rail 2 (HS2) project in full from London Euston to Manchester.

Amend the devolution settlement for Wales to remove powers over speed limits, I want the Government to amend powers devolved to the Welsh Senedd and Welsh Government as to remove control over speed limits. Ban Loyalty Card Schemes at all Supermarkets, We are worried by the trend of supermarkets implementing so-called ‘loyalty card schemes’. Ban the sale of all non-silent fireworks, Ban the sale and possession of fireworks to the general public unless they're silent. Add the highway code to the national curriculum, We think the basic principles of the highway code should be taught in key stage 2 and should be revisited in key stage 3 and 4., It is something that is necessary for everyone to know about, including pedestrians and cyclists - not just drivers. Only allow sale and use of fireworks on 5 November and New Year's Eve, Stop the sale and use of fireworks apart from for the 5th of November and New Year's Eve due to people using them too frequently. Only allow fireworks on the dates of traditional celebratory events, For the Government to only allow fireworks to be used on the date of traditional celebratory events such as November 5th, New Years, Diwali and Chinese New Year.
